title: MemTrapBench: Benchmarking Cognitive Traps in LLM Memory Use
abstract: arXiv:2608.20202v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Memory has become a key component of large language models, enabling them to retain information and learn from long-term interactions. However, existing memory benchmarks mainly evaluate whether information is correctly extracted, stored, and retrieved, while largely overlooking how retrieved memories reshape model reasoning and affect performance on the current task. We identify memory-induced cognitive traps: even faithfully recorded and semantically relevant memories can distort model reasoning or beliefs and degrade current task performance. To systematically evaluate these failure modes, we introduce MemTrapBench, which covers two forms of cognitive traps: Reasoning Fixation and Belief Distortion. translated_title: MemTrapBench：大语言模型记忆使用中的认知陷阱基准测试
translated_abstract: 摘要：记忆已成为大语言模型的关键组成部分，使其能够保留信息并从长期交互中学习。然而，现有的记忆基准主要评估信息是否正确提取、存储和检索，而很大程度上忽视了检索到的记忆如何重塑模型推理并影响当前任务的表现。我们识别出记忆引发的认知陷阱：即使是忠实记录且语义相关的记忆，也可能扭曲模型的推理或信念，并降低当前任务的表现。为了系统地评估这些失败模式，我们引入了MemTrapBench，它涵盖两种形式的认知陷阱：推理固化和信念扭曲。跨两个模型家族和五种代表性记忆框架的实验表明，MemTrapBench具有挑战性：所有评估的记忆策略均不如无记忆设置，即使是最强的方法也遭受性能下降。
tldr: 本文提出了MemTrapBench基准，揭示了即使正确检索的记忆也可能引发认知陷阱（推理固化和信念扭曲），并证明现有记忆策略在基准上均表现不佳。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces MemTrapBench, revealing that even correctly retrieved memories can induce cognitive traps (reasoning fixation and belief distortion), and demonstrates that all existing memory strategies underperform on this benchmark.
